newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes improvement in Korean relations.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes improvement in Korean relations.

text.p: China welcomed on Monday North Korea's apology over a submarine incursion into South Korean waters in September and said it hoped for further relaxation and new progress in the new year.

However, Beijing stopped short of a direct response to an invitation last April by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korea's President Kim Young-sam to take part in four-party talks with Pyongyang to secure a lasting peace to replace the truce that ended the Korean War.

"China welcomes efforts made by the parties concerned to remove as early as possible the effects of the submarine incident on the Korean Peninsula and to improve their mutual relations and maintain peace and stability of the Peninsula," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said on Monday.
China hoped the situation on the Korean Peninsula would move further towards relaxation in the coming new year, Shen said after being asked to comment on Pyongyang's apology on Sunday.
China hoped the parties concerned would continue to make progress in their dialogues and consultations, Shen said.
In a gesture of conciliation, the remains of 24 North Korean submarine intruders shot in the South were handed back across the border on Monday after Pyongyang's apology.

Seoul swiftly agreed to send home the remains after Pyongyang expressed "deep regret" on Sunday for the incursion by a North Korean submarine in September. It was an uprecedented statement of contrition towards the South.

Of 26 North Koreans that landed from the vessel, 11 were found shot dead -- apparently in a mass suicide -- and 13 were killed by Southern forces during a massive manhunt. One was captured alive and one is still at large.
U.S. President Bill Clinton hailed North Korea's apology as a move towards peace.

The submarine incursion put on ice last April's peace initiative, froze international food aid to the hungry North and stalled implementation of an agreement under which Pyongyang pledged to halt its nuclear weapons programme.
